title: LIDC: A Location Independent Multi-Cluster Computing Framework for Data Intensive Science
problem: Current multi-cluster computing relies on centralized Kubernetes controllers unsuitable for multi-organizational collaborations, requiring manual platform-specific configurations that cannot dynamically adapt to changing infrastructure.
motivation: Scientific collaborations require decentralized compute placement strategies that work across organizational boundaries without manual reconfiguration.
method: LIDC uses a decentralized control plane (a management system spread across multiple locations rather than centralized) that assigns meaningful names to computational tasks and matches them to available computing resources labeled with those same names. When new clusters or computers join the system, they automatically become available to accept matching tasks without requiring manual configuration or advance setup. This allows the system to adapt to changing infrastructure—adding or removing resources—without disrupting work.
key_novelty: The system decouples computational placement from specific clusters by using semantic names as a universal matching mechanism, enabling multi-organizational collaborations without predefined cluster assignments.
contributions: Decentralized control plane for multi-cluster compute placement
Semantic naming scheme for location-independent computation routing
Dynamic adaptation without prior knowledge of cluster configuration
